summary.text: Enid Uwimana is the Family First candidate for Ashwood at the 2026 Victorian election. On her party page she says she moved to Australia in 2014 to study at Deakin University, completing a Doctorate of Business Administration there in 2018 after a master's degree in audit management at Birmingham City University. Before that she worked in Rwanda for the Rwanda Revenue Authority and as director of internal audit at the National Bank of Rwanda, and she is president of the Rwandan Community Abroad in Victoria.

occupation.text: Auditor; formerly director of internal audit, National Bank of Rwanda

prior_roles.role: Tax auditor, later internal audit manager

priorities.text: Protect human life from conception to natural death
Empower individuals, families and communities to settle local matters themselves

sources.title: Dr. Enid Uwimana, Family First Party Australia
Ashwood District candidates, Victorian Electoral Commission

summary.text: Hitendra K. Joshi is running as a community independent for Ashwood at the 2026 Victorian election, endorsed by the local group Voices For Ashwood. He grew up in Pune, India, spent about ten years working in the Gulf, and moved to Australia with his family in 2017; he has worked for over 27 years as an electrical engineer on infrastructure and energy projects. His campaign puts government accountability first, alongside cost of living, community safety, climate action and local train services.

priorities.text: A properly funded, independent IBAC, a royal commission into the Big Build and open procurement
Lower household bills through less waste, a bigger return from mining royalties and cheaper renewables
More police on local streets and quicker help for people facing domestic violence
Better and more reliable services on the Glen Waverley and Alamein train lines
Being your elected representative is a responsibility, not a career path.

sources.title: Ashwood: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Hitendra Joshi, Independent for Ashwood (campaign site)

summary.text: Jacob van der Eynden is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Ashwood at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC's guide he grew up in Mount Waverley, is a student and digital media designer, has worked in local shops and cafes, and organises with the Campaign Against Racism and Fascism. His party page carried no biography as at early November 2026.

sources.title: Ashwood: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Jacob van der Eynden, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Matt Fregon is a Labor MP who won Mount Waverley in 2018 and has represented Ashwood since that district was created in 2022. He has been Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly since December 2022. He is standing again in Ashwood in 2026.

occupation.text: Owner and manager of a small IT business

prior_roles.role: Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
Deputy Government Whip in the Assembly

summary.text: Steven Mitchell is the One Nation candidate for Ashwood at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide describes him as an IT professional of more than 25 years' standing whose work has spanned software development, project management and training. It adds that he helps out at a local primary school and trains players at a local football club.

sources.title: Ashwood: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Theo Zographos is the Liberal candidate for Ashwood at the 2026 Victorian election. He was a Monash City councillor from 2012 to 2024 and works in corporate banking as a relationship manager at ANZ. He stood for Oakleigh as the Liberal candidate in 2014, losing to Labor's Steve Dimopoulos, and in 2024 the Liberals dropped him as their pick for the federal seat of Chisholm in favour of Katie Allen.

previous_candidacies.note: No source gives the label he ran under; Wikipedia's councillor table lists him as Liberal. The party page says he was elected three times but gives no years for the later two.

priorities.text: Safer streets, lower costs and better government under the Liberals' Fresh Start platform

sources.title: Ashwood: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Theo Zographos, Liberal for Ashwood, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Tim Randall is the Greens candidate for Ashwood at the 2026 Victorian election. An architect whose work focuses on accessible housing, he grew up in Hobart and has lived in Melbourne's eastern suburbs for more than 15 years. He contested the federal seat of Chisholm for the Greens in 2025, taking 12.5% of the primary vote.

priorities.text: my commitment to protecting the environment and strengthening our communities
